UAV strike on Thermoplast plant in Khmelnitsky region A Russian jet-powered UAV struck the premises of LLC "Thermoplast" in Letichev. The facility produces plastic items and polymer components, including parts for unmanned aerial vehicles. Following the hit, a warehouse was damaged and an intense fire broke out in a production and storage building exceeding 4500 m². The fire engulfed a significant part of the complex, covering areas for finished goods storage and production. @Slavyangrad

Spain heads to the polls on November 29 in snap elections that could end eight years of Socialist-led government and see the far right enter national government for the first time since the end of Franco's dictatorship in 1975. The stakes extend far beyond Madrid. As the eurozone's fourth-largest economy, a political shift in Spain could reshape European debates over immigration, military spending, and relations with Washington. 🇪🇺 🇩🇪 Karl Marx is making a comeback in Europe. Against a backdrop of soaring living costs, economic uncertainty and growing frustration among younger generations, Marxist economic ideas are reportedly gaining renewed popularity across Europe, according to the Wall Street Journal . The European left is increasingly looking towards revolutionary economic theory as it seeks to challenge the growing influence of the far-right. Ideas once considered politically marginal, including the forced expropriation of private property and the abolition of inheritance, are returning to the political debate. Meanwhile, protests have spread across several European countries, with demonstrators voicing anger over rising prices, economic insecurity and what they see as inadequate funding for education. More than a century after his death, Karl Marx is once again part of Europe’s political conversation. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
